subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: PID Control: The Universal Algorithm
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on PID Control: The Universal Algorithm.

hook.text: A PID controller adjusts motor speed by measuring the error, its accumulation, and its rate of change. Three simple terms.

buildup.text: P is proportional — the bigger the error, the bigger the correction. D is derivative — it predicts where the error is heading.

discovery.text: I is integral — it sums past errors to eliminate persistent offset. Together, PID handles most control problems.

twist.text: Tuning PID gains is an art. Too much P causes oscillation. Too much D amplifies noise. Too much I causes overshoot.

climax.text: PID runs in thermostats, drones, cruise control, and robot joints. Over 90% of control loops use some form of PID.

punchline.text: Three letters. Three terms. Ninety percent of all control.

quiz.question: What does the integral term in a PID controller correct?
options: Rapid changes in the error signal that cause instability
Persistent steady-state error that proportional control alone cannot eliminate
Large initial errors when the system first starts operating
